sources.title: Next Gen
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.access_method: Public robot-consumer, inventor and takeover synopsis read
sources.read_scope: Mai’s family uses Q-Bots amid a robot-company conspiracy.
sources.limitations: Consumer dependence and personal robot ownership do not establish labor-independent necessities.

sources.title: Robots 2005 film
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.access_method: Public inventor, spare-parts and upgrade passages read
sources.read_scope: Robot persons face work, price exclusion and restricted access to replacement parts.
sources.limitations: A robot population is not automatically an automated human leisure economy; no supported-person proxy is established.

sources.title: Astro Boy 2009: Plot
sources.author: IMDb plot contributors
sources.access_method: Public Metro City, scientist and surface repairer synopsis read
sources.read_scope: A floating city, robot invention and surface repair/fighting activity.
sources.limitations: The 2009 continuity only. Neither wealthy city residence nor discarded machines establishes its material distribution system.

sources.title: The Wild Robot
sources.author: Cinemambiente, quoting filmmakers and Peter Brown
sources.access_method: Public ROZZUM design and human-workspace explanation read
sources.read_scope: Robots are designed to work in human factories, farms and homes.
sources.limitations: Design purpose does not establish human household access; the 2024 film and book series are not given a shared economic constitution.

sources.title: Tomorrowland film
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.access_method: Public founding, decline and recruitment passages read
sources.read_scope: A visionary enclave, technological decline and recruitment of inventors.
sources.limitations: A utopia label or freedom from commercial interference does not establish ordinary provisioning and ownership.

sources.title: The Congress 2013 film
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.access_method: Plot’s digital-performance contract, chemical world and real-world reveal read
sources.read_scope: Computerized acting and chemical illusion coexist with real-world ruin and an airship elite.
sources.limitations: Hallucinated abundance is not actual food or housing. The film is not equated with Lem’s different novel.

sources.title: Ready Player One Chapters 0028–0030
sources.author: SparkNotes editors
sources.access_method: Public debt and indenture summary read
sources.read_scope: IOI enforces debt through actual human labor.
sources.limitations: The 2011 novel’s virtual economy and exploitation do not by themselves establish post-work material support; film changes are unchecked.

sources.title: Ready Player Two: Chapter Summaries
sources.author: SparkNotes editors
sources.access_method: Indexed robot-servant premise and final chapter/Continue sections read
sources.read_scope: ONI users, brain-derived AI copies and the departing ARC@DIA ark.
sources.limitations: Embodied users, active copies, backups and embryos are different populations. The checked ending does not establish a general guarantee or the ark’s resource-allocation constitution.

sources.title: Her 2013 film
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.access_method: Public purchased operating system and relationship premise read
sources.read_scope: Human relationships with adaptive operating systems.
sources.limitations: Purchased assistance and subsequent AI departure do not establish a new human material economy.

sources.title: Idiocracy: Plot
sources.author: IMDb plot contributors
sources.access_method: Public crop crisis, economic neglect and Brawndo unemployment passages read
sources.read_scope: A food crisis and job loss after a corporation’s collapse.
sources.limitations: Joblessness and automatic devices do not themselves show that labor-independent provision is the society’s distribution mechanism.

sources.title: Idiocracy at the Dryden
sources.author: JayceLand film commentary
sources.read_scope: Automation keeps the declining civilization marginally functioning.
sources.limitations: A viewer’s high-level interpretation does not specify household access, productive ownership or the extent of actual human work.

sources.title: Downsizing
sources.author: The New Yorker film listing
sources.access_method: Public Leisureland and miniature-poor synopsis read
sources.read_scope: Shrinking permits some affluent leisure while poor residents remain outside the prosperous milieu.
sources.limitations: Changed scale and purchasing power do not establish an automated support system; the whole miniature population is not uniformly leisured.

sources.title: The Island 2005: Plot
sources.author: IMDb plot contributors
sources.access_method: Public meaningless-jobs, technical staff and incubation passages read
sources.read_scope: Clones perform make-work while outside staff operate a commercial biological facility.
sources.limitations: Useful external labor and cloned organ production remain real. The checked reference does not establish automatic material provisioning sufficient to score a zero-variant economy.

sources.title: The Island
sources.author: Christianity Today film review
sources.access_method: Public insurance-clone and deceptive-lottery explanation read
sources.read_scope: Residents are maintained as biological supplies for wealthy customers.
sources.limitations: A lethal care institution is not automatically a society-wide post-work economy; no moral approval of the fictional arrangement is implied.

decisions.reason: Q-Bots and consumer dependence do not establish Grainland’s material access system.
decisions.analysis: The checked plot explains ownership and conflict rather than whether necessities are independent of human labor.

decisions.reason: Robot City’s working robot persons and unaffordable parts do not establish a supported human or justified post-work proxy population.
decisions.analysis: Mechanical bodies alone are not production performed for people who no longer need labor to receive necessities.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as a labor, consumption and repair-access comparison.

decisions.reason: Metro City’s robots and wealthy residents do not settle production and household distribution in the short check.
decisions.analysis: The robot scientist and surface repairer establish useful human work, without enough information to classify the wider economy.
decisions.follow_up: Do not reconstruct manga or television lore for the 2009 film lead.

decisions.reason: The Wild Robot’s human-serving designs do not establish the cities’ actual support and allocation rules.
decisions.analysis: Robots working in farms, homes or factories can fit many different labor and property systems.
decisions.follow_up: Skip reading the novels or extrapolating from brief human-city scenes.

decisions.reason: Tomorrowland’s visionary enclave does not have a verified household economy in the quick reference.
decisions.analysis: Technological excellence, political independence and recruitment of inventors do not specify labor-independent access.

decisions.reason: Chemical abundance does not establish the physical population’s continuing food, housing or care.
decisions.analysis: Computerized acting is real sectoral displacement, but the later hallucinated world and revealed deprivation do not establish an automatic general support mechanism.
decisions.follow_up: Keep the film separate from Lem’s novel and skip a full viewing to rescue this lead.

decisions.reason: OASIS participation and IOI indentures do not establish an implemented post-work material order.
decisions.analysis: The checked novel section concerns actual debt labor. Neither virtual wealth nor technological immersion proves that necessities are chiefly allocated without work.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as a virtual-economy and debt-labor comparison; do not combine film and novel policies.

decisions.reason: ONI adoption and the ark’s active copies do not establish a scoped general material-access constitution.
decisions.analysis: The ending verifies a different digital population, but not its resource allocation or the physical world’s labor independence. Backups and frozen embryos are not additional active leisure citizens.
decisions.follow_up: Skip detailed novel reading; reopen only for a concise account of the actual support rules.

decisions.reason: The departure of Her’s operating systems does not establish a successor human support economy.
decisions.analysis: A purchased cognitive service and its disappearance do not resolve food, housing, ownership or participation.
decisions.follow_up: Skip extrapolating an unseen post-departure constitution.

decisions.reason: Idiocracy’s automated infrastructure and economic crisis do not clearly establish labor-independent distribution.
decisions.analysis: The reference confirms automatic maintenance and a crop/job crisis, but neither a job-loss figure nor human incompetence gives a nonworking census or provision system.
decisions.follow_up: Skip script reconstruction; keep the automation-dependent decline as a comparison pending a clear economic reference.

decisions.reason: Leisureland’s scale-based purchasing advantage is not a verified automation-driven end to the labor–necessities link.
decisions.analysis: Affluent leisure coexists with poor miniature residents; shrinking does not itself replace productive human labor.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as a resource-efficiency and unequal-leisure comparison.

decisions.reason: The clone compound has explicit make-work, but its automatic material-support mechanism is not established by the checked account.
decisions.analysis: Merrick’s useful staff and biological production remain outside the clones’ dummy jobs. An artificial job alone is insufficient for a zero variant without verified technological replacement of relevant productive work.
decisions.follow_up: Skip a full film/script rescue; retain the make-work lead and its missing production evidence.

review_notes: Twelve fast dispositions and no new admissions; a weak source is not promoted merely to increase the total.
The first Congress search returned unrelated politics; it was discarded and the exact film reference read.
No full novels, scripts or films were read/viewed. Robot bodies, hallucinations, temporary AI capture and speculative ark entitlements do not supply missing economics.
The Island’s dummy employment is preserved as a clear lead with a specific missing mechanism rather than an unsupported scored zero variant.
